info.title: Portos API
info.description: The Portos API is for turning on lights, playing music on your speaker, and managing your devices.

tags.name: OAuth flows
tags.description:
Use OAuth flows to sign a person or an agent in to Port OS and get an
access token for the other APIs.

Port OS requires authorization for calls against its APIs. It uses OAuth
to issue the tokens that authorize those calls, and it supports
extensions that let agents connect automatically: Dynamic Client
Registration, client information metadata documents, PKCE and others.

This section covers discovery metadata, client registration, authorize
and consent, and the callback that returns the authorization code.
Registration alone grants no access to resources. Operation scopes
restrict delegated authority in addition to the permission rules for
principals and resources.

tags.name: Tokens
tags.description:
Use tokens when you already have credentials and need an access token,
or when you want to manage the long-lived tokens you hand to a CLI,
device automation or agent.

Tokens are JWTs vended by principals for token exchange. A principal may
create tokens, and list and delete the tokens it owns. The raw JWT is
returned only once at creation. Exchange it at the OAuth token endpoint
for an access token, then refresh or revoke the grant there.

tags.name: Principals
tags.description:
Use principals when you manage who can act in Port OS.

Principals are people, endpoints, or organizations. They can perform
actions on resources, and can be granted permissions to access
resources.

tags.name: Secrets
tags.description:
Use secrets to store a credential that Port OS needs to keep for you, such
as a key a plugin uses to call a provider.

A secret is a type of storage credential.

tags.name: Clients
tags.description:
Use clients when you build an application that signs in to Port OS with
OAuth and need to register it, rotate its secrets, or remove it.

Clients are applications that can interact with Port OS.

tags.name: Access control
tags.description:
Use access control to decide who can do what with a resource.

Rules grant or deny permissions on a resource to principals. You can also
evaluate a rule to check what a principal is allowed to do.

tags.name: Endpoints
tags.description:
An endpoint is a device or service you can act on, such as a phone, TV,
lightbulb or vacuum.

Customers interact with endpoints whenever they want to control their
lights or find where their phone is.

Endpoints declare a set of capabilities. These capabilities denote what
functions an endpoint has. For example, an endpoint that declares the
power interface can be turned on and off. Similarly, the capability tells
customers they can check whether the device is on or off.

tags.name: Messages
tags.description:
Port OS allows you to send messages to things. 
By sending messages to endpoints, customers can turn off lights, play music, etc. 
A message is an object that is sent around in port OS between different endpoints.

tags.name: Plugins
tags.description:
A plugin is a receiver of messages. A plugin could be an HTTP connection, android device messenger, an MQTT connection, or anything else.
Messages sent to endpoints are propagated through plugins.

tags.name: Routes
tags.description:
A route is a part of an endpoint that denotes what types of interfaces the endpoint can support from a specific plugin. 
Additionally, a route may describe the endpoint with metadata such as names, manufacturer name, model data, etc.

tags.name: Endpoint Simulators
tags.description: Endpoint Simulators lets customers simulate endpoints to test out their flows and integrations.

tags.name: Subscriptions
tags.description:
When a message gets sent to port OS, you may want to listen to it. 

Customers can enable a subscription for a customer's events, and have the subscription published to a flow, a plugin, or endpoint. 

This makes it so that subscriptions can trigger events.

get.description:
List the endpoints that a customer has access to. For example, you
enumerate to list the customer's lights, vacuums, or similar devices.

Endpoints contain information such as:
  1. The endpoint's name, description, and other top-level data.
  2. The capabilities the endpoint has, like power, camera, etc.
  3. The state of the endpoint.

Usage of the API is controlled by the query parameters. By default it
lists enabled endpoints owned by the authenticated user. Type and
serialNumber filters stay within that scope. An explicit owner can select
another owner's endpoints when the caller can read them.

An exact id lookup takes precedence over the owner, type, serialNumber, and
enablement filters. It can return a readable shared endpoint, including a
disabled one, but still requires endpoint-read permission.

To retrieve the state of a specific endpoint, send `id=<endpoint-id>`
together with `expand=interfaces.attributes`. Add
`forceDeviceAttributeQuery=true` to refresh that state from the device
before the response is returned.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of a specific endpoint to retrieve. When provided, this exact-ID filter takes precedence over owner, type, serialNumber and enablement filters. It can return a shared or disabled endpoint when the caller has endpoint-read permission.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter endpoints by their primary type

parameters.name: serialNumber
parameters.description: Filter endpoints by their serial number

parameters.name: nextToken
parameters.description: Opaque server-issued continuation token. Repeat the same selection, page size, expansion, force-refresh setting and authenticated grant. Modified, expired or differently bound tokens return 400; restart without nextToken.

parameters.name: maxResults
parameters.description: The maximum number of results to return, from 1 through 100.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Expand determines what data we retrieve for each endpoint.

Use `interfaces.attributes` to populate each endpoint's `attributes`
array so you can, for example, find their states.

When omitted, the response returns only a limited set of data.

parameters.name: forceDeviceAttributeQuery
parameters.description:
Forces a live device-backed attribute refresh for endpoint-state
queries.

This makes Port OS call into the device to get its data, if the device
provider does not update the state automatically.

This flag is only applied when `expand` includes
`interfaces.attributes`. Send `true` to force the refresh; absent or
`false` values use stored state. Invalid values, or `true` without
the required expansion, return 400.

200.description: Endpoints retrieved successfully. Responses without `expand=interfaces.attributes` return the default shallow endpoint shape. Responses with that expansion populate deep attribute state in each endpoint's `attributes` array. If endpoint enumeration succeeds but one or more forced deep-query items fail, the response can include an `errors` array describing those partial state-refresh failures; request-level failures still use HTTP error responses.

post.description: Creates or updates a route.

Triggers route synchronization for a plugin.
When a plugin connected to Port OS wants to report the routes available on it, it dispatches a discovery payload. The server reconciles the reported routes with its internal state.
For newly persisted synchronized routes, the server can assign a backend-generated, owner-scoped Port OS route `id`; a client-supplied route `id` in the discovery payload is advisory and is not the stable lookup surface for plugin capability parity. Consumers that need to match synchronized plugin or fixture routes after enumeration should use `associatedPluginRouteId`, which preserves the plugin-owned route identity.
Every route and group-route interface must name a capability interface and exact version from the capability-interface library, its `configuration` must conform to that interface's configuration schema (an omitted configuration is validated as an empty object), and any declared attribute must exist on the interface with a value that conforms to its attribute schema. Any nonconforming item rejects the whole request with 400; `errors` lists every rejected item keyed by `pluginRouteId`. Nothing is persisted.
Group routes and relationships are keyed by plugin-owned identity within the plugin and auth link and are created or updated, never removed because they are omitted. A `pluginRouteId` must be unique across routes and group routes (`PLUGIN_ROUTE_ID_CONFLICT`). Group-route members and relationship vertices must resolve to routes or group routes of the same plugin and auth link, committed or in the same request (`UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE`).
`IS_PART_OF` joins two group routes and is acyclic (`RELATIONSHIP_CYCLE`) with at most one parent per group route (`MULTIPLE_PARENTS`); `CAN_CONTROL` and `LOCATED_IN` join a route to a group route; self-edges and other shapes are `INVALID_RELATIONSHIP`. Only `CAN_CONTROL` carries `interfaces`, which must name interfaces and inbound messages the source route declares (`MESSAGE_UNSUPPORTED`). Relationship items are keyed by `relationshipExternalId`.
A newly reported group route creates its own endpoint group named after it; rediscovery keeps group IDs, merges and user renames.
Requires a signed user/session or the existing authenticated client flow. The anonymous DCR delegated device profile cannot invoke this operation.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Client-chosen key that makes a non-idempotent request retry-safe, following draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header. A committed response is stored for 24 hours and replayed for the same principal, operation, key and payload. Missing key returns 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED, a key longer than 255 characters returns 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID, the same key with a different payload returns 422, and the same key while the first request is still in flight returns 409. Failed (rolled-back) requests do not consume the key.

The mutation is applied only when it still matches: a stale value returns 412 PRECONDITION_FAILED and a missing header returns 428 PRECONDITION_REQUIRED. `*` matches any current version of an existing group (RFC 9110), for a deliberate last-writer-wins change.

Subscription.description: A subscription is a way to listen to events

id.description: The unique identifier for the subscription

context.description: Structured filter criteria for granular device event matching. Keys are dot-notation paths into the message (e.g., "header.namespace", "header.name"). Values are the expected values to match. All context entries must match for the subscription to fire. Omitting context matches all events.

reasonCode.description: Redacted stable lifecycle reason, when applicable.

eventQueryProfile.description: Supported typed event query validation profile, when this is an event monitor.

SynchronizationRequest.description: Request payload for synchronizing plugin routes, group routes and their relationships with the system. When a route in this payload includes `id`, that value is advisory for synchronization and is not the stable identifier to assert after enumeration unless a specific implementation documents preservation. Newly persisted synchronized routes can receive backend-generated, owner-scoped Port OS route IDs; use each route's `associatedPluginRouteId` to match the stable plugin-owned or fixture route identity. Omitted group routes and relationships are not deletion instructions. Every reference must resolve to committed data or to an item in the same request.

authLinkIdentity.description: The ID of the auth link

routes.description: List of routes to synchronize. Route `id` values supplied here are not the stable plugin capability lookup surface after synchronization; match enumerated routes by `associatedPluginRouteId`.

groupRoutes.description: Group routes (maps, rooms, provider groups) to create or update, keyed by `pluginRouteId` within the plugin and auth link.

relationships.description: Typed relationships between the reported routes and group routes.

GroupRoute.description: A provider-reported group route (for example a vacuum map or room, a lighting room or a speaker group) as carried by discovery. It is shared by the route-discovery report message and `SynchronizationRequest.groupRoutes` so both decode to the same model.

pluginProfileId.description: Stable group-route profile ID selected from the registered V2 plugin declaration.

ontologicalTypes.description: Actual classifications of the native group route, constrained by its selected plugin profile for V2 discovery.

pluginRouteId.description: Plugin-owned stable identifier of the group route. Must be unique across routes and group routes within one plugin and auth link.

name.description: The name of the associated group route

memberPluginRouteIds.description: List of plugin route IDs that are members of this group route

pluginCustomMetadata.description: Private plugin metadata (native map, segment or cloud room addressing) returned to the plugin on dispatch; never exposed as application data.

PluginDiscoveryRelationship.description: A provider-reported relationship between typed port resources. Identity is `externalId` within the reporting plugin and auth link; resubmitting the same `externalId` updates the relationship. Omission from a later synchronization is not a deletion instruction.

externalId.description: Plugin-owned stable identifier of the relationship.

interfaces.description: Optional interface applicability; used by `CAN_CONTROL` to declare which messages the source supports on the target.

PluginDiscoveryRelationshipVertex.description: One end of a discovered relationship, addressed by plugin-owned identity within the reporting plugin and auth link. Exactly one of `pluginRouteId` (a route), `groupPluginRouteId` (a group route), `endpointId` or `groupId` must be set.

pluginRouteId.description: The plugin route ID of a route reported in the same or an earlier synchronization.

groupPluginRouteId.description: The plugin route ID of a group route reported in the same or an earlier synchronization.

endpointId.description: The full ID of an endpoint owned by the reporting principal.

groupId.description: The full ID of a group owned by the reporting principal.

RelationshipType.description: Typed relationship between port resources. `IS_PART_OF`: a resource is contained in a parent resource (acyclic). `CAN_CONTROL`: an endpoint or route can act on another resource with the listed interface messages; it never grants authorization. `LOCATED_IN`: an endpoint route is currently observed inside a group route; it is an observation, not membership. `MEMBER_OF`: an endpoint belongs to a group.

RelationshipInterface.description: Capability-interface applicability of a relationship, for example the robotic-vacuum-cleaner messages a `CAN_CONTROL` edge supports on a room.

messages.description: Message names of the interface the relationship applies to. An explicit empty array applies to no messages. Omission retains every message supported by the source interface.

ErrorDetails.description: Optional typed context for an error. Fields are additive and only populated when the error can safely expose that context to API clients.

endpointId.description: Port OS endpoint ID involved in the failed dispatch.

pluginId.description: Port OS plugin ID that reported the failure.

pluginRouteId.description: Plugin-owned route identifier involved in the failed dispatch.

provider.description: Third-party provider or bridge name that reported the failure.

directive.description: Message namespace and name or provider directive that failed.

actual.description: String representation of the submitted value when the plugin can safely report it.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Suggested retry delay for rate-limit or provider-unavailable failures.

correlationId.description: Provider or plugin correlation ID useful for support.

providerCode.description: The third-party provider's own error code, for support. It is opaque and provider-specific; branch on `code` and `family` instead.

correlationToken.description: Token that correlates an outcome-unknown dispatch with its eventual result.

fieldErrors.description: The request fields that were rejected, when the error is about the request's content.

ErrorFieldError.description: One rejected request field of an error.

field.description: Name or JSON path of the rejected field.

reason.description: Why the field was rejected and what an accepted value looks like.

Error.description: The one Port OS error shape, returned by every REST error response and every MCP tool error. `code` names the specific failure and `family` its broad class; both are closed enums, so clients branch on them and show `message`, which says what failed and what to do next.

message.description: Plain-language description of the failure and the suggested next action.

errors.description: Every rejected item when a request that is validated item by item and applied atomically fails, such as a discovery `SynchronizationRequest` whose routes, group routes or relationships are rejected. Omitted for single-item failures.

ErrorCode.description: The specific error, one of a closed set of Port OS codes. Every REST error body, MCP tool error, batch item error and discovery item error uses this enum; each code belongs to an `ErrorFamily` that decides its HTTP status. Provider-specific codes are never codes: they travel in `details.providerCode`. New failure kinds are added here, never as free strings.

ErrorFamily.description: The broad class of an error. The family decides the HTTP status of a REST error, so clients can handle every code of a family alike.

AuthResourceType.description: Port OS resource types that can be used for permission evaluation, scoped authorization, OAuth grants, and access-control resources.

Query.description: Shared Port OS query AST modeled as a recursive JSON graph supporting match, comparison, pattern, freeform, and boolean operators.

and.description: match all fields in the array

freeformMatch.description: Freeform query string for natural language searches

not.description: Negate the inner query (NOT wraps a single child query)

id.description: The unique identifier for the endpoint group

name.description: The name of the endpoint group

ownerId.description: The ID of the owner of the endpoint group

redirectedFrom.description: Set when the group was read through a merged-away ID: the ID that was requested, which now redirects to this group. Mutations must use this group's `id`.

parentGroupId.description: The canonical parent group derived from `IS_PART_OF` relationships, when the group has one.

childGroupIds.description: Canonical child groups derived from `IS_PART_OF` relationships.

controllers.description: Endpoints that declare `CAN_CONTROL` on one of this group's group routes, with the messages they support on it.

attributes.description: The group's state: every attribute value stored for its group routes, one entry per group route and attribute, tagged with the group route and provider. Populated only when the read is called with `expand=interfaces.attributes`.

ontologicalTypes.description: Actual classifications of this native group route.

associatedGroupId.description: The ID of the associated endpoint group

associatedPluginId.description: The ID of the associated plugin

ownerId.description: The ID of the owner of the group route

memberPluginRouteIds.description: List of member plugin route IDs of the group route

interfaces.description: List of interfaces supported by the group route

pluginCustomMetadata.description: A set of custom metadata that the plugin uses and attaches to the group route, this is meant specifically for the plugin to use.

interfaces.description: Interfaces and messages the endpoint supports on the group.

groupRouteId.description: The typed ID of the group route the value was reported for.

pluginId.description: The plugin that owns the group route and reported the value.

namespace.description: The capability interface namespace for this attribute

value.description: The attribute value payload, structure depends on the attribute schema

sampledAt.description: When the provider observed the value. Omitted when the provider did not say.

etag.description: The group's `etag` as last read by the client.

EndpointGroupRedirect.description: A merged-away group ID and the group it now redirects to. Reads and control follow redirects; mutations fail with GROUP_MERGED.

EndpointGroupsManageOperationType.description: Discriminator of an endpoint group management operation.

EndpointGroupsCreateGroupOperation.description: Creates a user group. Its new ID and etag are returned in the result; later operations in the same batch cannot reference it. A user group name is `{"type": "PLAIN", "value": ...}` whose value is non-blank UTF-8 text of at most 256 bytes with no control characters; anything else is rejected with BAD_REQUEST. Each added member must be the ID of an existing endpoint the caller can read; a malformed ID is BAD_REQUEST, and a missing or unreadable endpoint is NOT_FOUND.

etag.description: The group etag the client last read. When an earlier operation in the same request changes this group, send the etag that operation reports instead: every operation that changes the group advances its etag by one, and one that changes nothing keeps it.

EndpointGroupsSetNameOperation.description: Renames a group. The name is a user override that survives rediscovery. A user group name is `{"type": "PLAIN", "value": ...}` whose value is non-blank UTF-8 text of at most 256 bytes with no control characters; anything else is rejected with BAD_REQUEST.

etag.description: The group etag the client last read. When an earlier operation in the same request changes this group, send the etag that operation reports instead: every operation that changes the group advances its etag by one, and one that changes nothing keeps it.

EndpointGroupsAddMembersOperation.description: Adds endpoint members to a group. Each added member must be the ID of an existing endpoint the caller can read; a malformed ID is BAD_REQUEST, and a missing or unreadable endpoint is NOT_FOUND.

etag.description: The group etag the client last read. When an earlier operation in the same request changes this group, send the etag that operation reports instead: every operation that changes the group advances its etag by one, and one that changes nothing keeps it.

EndpointGroupsRemoveMembersOperation.description: Removes endpoint members from a group. IDs that are not members are ignored.

etag.description: The group etag the client last read. When an earlier operation in the same request changes this group, send the etag that operation reports instead: every operation that changes the group advances its etag by one, and one that changes nothing keeps it.

EndpointGroupsMergeIntoOperation.description: Merges source groups into a target group. Source group routes are rehomed to the target, memberships are unioned, and each source ID becomes a redirect to the target. Identity decision that requires explicit user confirmation.

sources.description: Groups merged into the target; each must be distinct from the target and from each other.

EndpointGroupsManageOperation.description: One endpoint group management operation, discriminated by `operation`. Unknown operations are rejected with 400.

EndpointGroupsManageRequest.description: Atomic batch of static endpoint group management operations. Operations are applied in order inside one transaction; either all commit or none do. `requestId` values must be unique within the request. Physical control is never part of this request. Every operation that writes a group advances its etag by one, so a later operation on a group already written in the same request must send the etag the earlier operation reports; each result reports the group's etag right after its operation.

validateOnly.description: When true, runs authorization and validation and returns what would happen, writing nothing. A validate-only request neither requires nor consumes an `Idempotency-Key`.

EndpointGroupsManageResult.description: Result of one committed operation, correlated by `requestId`. `CREATE_GROUP`, `SET_NAME`, `ADD_MEMBERS` and `REMOVE_MEMBERS` return `group` with its new etag; `DELETE_GROUP` returns `deletedGroupId`; `MERGE_INTO` returns `target` with its new etag and `redirects`.

EndpointGroupsManageResponse.description: Atomic batch envelope. `errors` is empty if and only if the batch committed. On failure `results` is empty and `errors` lists every failing operation; nothing is written and no events are emitted. Items correlate by `requestId`, never by position.

Relationship.description: A typed relationship between port resources. Provider discovery and group membership operations manage relationships; the REST collection is read-only.

associatedPluginId.description: The plugin that reported the relationship.

RelationshipVertex.description: A typed resource at one end of a relationship. Route parents are endpoints; group-route parents are groups.

id.description: The full Port OS ID of this resource.

parentId.description: The full endpoint or group ID for a route or group-route vertex. Omitted for endpoint and group vertices.

RelationshipVertexKind.description: The resource kind addressed by a relationship vertex.

EnumerateRelationshipsResponse.description: Paginated response containing relationships visible to the caller.

errors.description: Partial query errors collected while returning available results.

BatchOperationRequestId.description: Client-chosen identifier for one operation in a batch request. It must be unique within the request and is echoed in the matching result or error so items are correlated by ID, never by position.

ReadinessStatus.description: Readiness of the server. `READY` means the server can sign tokens.

ReadinessResponse.description: Readiness of the server and the key that currently signs new tokens.

signingKeyId.description: Key ID (`kid`) of the key that signs new tokens, as published in the JWKS.

BatchResponseStatus.description: Outcome of an atomic batch. `COMMITTED` means every operation was applied (or, for a validate-only request, would be applied); `FAILED` means nothing was written and `errors` lists every failing operation.

BatchItemError.description: Error for one operation of an atomic batch, correlated by the operation's `requestId`. `status` is the HTTP status the operation would have returned on its own.

status.description: HTTP-equivalent status code of the item failure.

message.description: Plain-language description of the failure and the suggested next action.

resourceId.description: The resource the failure applies to, when it is not the operation's primary target.

SynchronizationItemError.description: One rejected discovery item of a `SynchronizationRequest`, keyed by the plugin-owned identity of the rejected item: `pluginRouteId` for a route or group route, or `relationshipExternalId` for a relationship. Exactly one of the two is set. It shares the `code`, `family`, `status` and `message` fields of `BatchItemError`; discovery items are keyed by plugin-owned identity because they carry no `requestId`. A request with any rejected item is rejected as a whole and lists every rejected item.

pluginRouteId.description: Plugin-owned identifier of the rejected route or group route. Set unless the item is a relationship.

relationshipExternalId.description: Plugin-owned `externalId` of the rejected relationship. Set only for relationship items.

interface.description: Canonical capability interface name the failure applies to, when the failure is interface-specific.

version.description: Declared capability interface version the failure applies to, when the failure is interface-specific.

status.description: HTTP-equivalent status code of the item failure.

message.description: Plain-language description of the failure and the suggested fix.

OAuthClient.description: An OAuth 2.0 client registration conforming to RFC 7591 with Port OS extensions.

id.description: Stable query result identifier for the OAuth client. Mirrors clientId.

clientId.description: The unique identifier for the OAuth client

clientName.description: A human-readable string name of the client to be presented to the end-user during authorization. If omitted, the authorization server may display the raw "client_id" value to the end-user instead. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

clientUri.description: A URL string of a web page providing information about the client. If present, the server should display this URL to the end-user in a clickable fashion. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

logoUri.description: A URL string that references a logo for the client. If present, the server should display this image to the end-user during approval. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

redirectUris.description: An array of redirection URI strings for use in redirect-based flows such as the authorization code and implicit flows. Clients using these flows must register their redirection URI values. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

allowedOrigins.description: An array of authorized JavaScript origin strings. When set, the server validates the Origin header on token requests against this list. Origins are scheme + host (+ optional port), with no path.

grantTypes.description: An array of OAuth 2.0 grant type strings that the client can use at the token endpoint. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

responseTypes.description: An array of OAuth 2.0 response type strings that the client can use at the authorization endpoint. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

tokenEndpointAuthMethod.description: A string indicating the requested authentication method for the token endpoint. Values defined by this specification are "client_secret_post", "client_secret_basic", "client_secret_jwt", "private_key_jwt", and "none". See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

tokenEndpointAuthSigningAlg.description: A string containing a JWS signing algorithm (alg value) that MUST be used for signing the JWT used to authenticate the client at the token endpoint for the "private_key_jwt" and "client_secret_jwt" authentication methods. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

scope.description: A string containing a space-separated list of scope values that the client can use when requesting access tokens. Valid scopes are: endpoint:read, endpoint:write, message:read, message:send, secret:read, secret:write, flow:read, flow:write, flow:trigger, principal:read, principal:write, subscription:read, subscription:write, access-control-rule:read, access-control-rule:write. Scopes are mapped to Cedar permissions (e.g., "endpoint:read" maps to "endpoint.read"). See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

scopes.description: List of OAuth scopes that this client can request (array representation of scope). This is a convenience field that represents the space-separated scope string as an array. Scopes are mapped to Cedar permissions (e.g., "endpoint:read" maps to "endpoint.read").

contacts.description: An array of strings representing ways to contact people responsible for this client, typically email addresses. The authorization server may make these contact addresses available to end-users for support requests for the client. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

tosUri.description: A URL string that points to a human-readable terms of service document for the client that describes a contractual relationship between the end-user and the client that the end-user accepts when authorizing the client. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

tosUriLocalized.description: Localized versions of the terms of service URI using language tags as keys (BCP 47 format). The keys are language tags and values are the localized terms of service URIs. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2.2

policyUri.description: A URL string that points to a human-readable privacy policy document that describes how the deployment organization collects, uses, retains, and discloses personal data. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

policyUriLocalized.description: Localized versions of the privacy policy URI using language tags as keys (BCP 47 format). The keys are language tags and values are the localized privacy policy URIs. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2.2

clientSecret.description: The client secret string known only to the client and the authorization server. This secret is used for authenticating the client to the authorization server. This field is typically only returned during client registration and should not be included in GET responses for security reasons. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2.2

clientSecretExpiresAt.description: An integer indicating the expiration time of the client secret, represented as the number of seconds since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z). A value of 0 indicates that the secret does not expire. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2.2

jwksUri.description: A URL string referencing the client's JSON Web Key (JWK) Set document, which contains the client's public keys. These keys can be used by higher-level protocols that use signing or encryption. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

jwks.description: The client's JSON Web Key Set document value, which contains the client's public keys. This parameter is intended to be used by clients that cannot use the "jwks_uri" parameter, such as native clients that cannot host public URLs. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

keys.description: The JSON Web Keys (RFC 7517) of the set.

softwareId.description: A unique identifier string assigned by the client developer or software publisher used by registration endpoints to identify the client software to be dynamically registered. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

softwareVersion.description: A version identifier string for the client software identified by "software_id". The value of the "software_version" should change on any update to the client software identified by the same "software_id". See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2

ownerId.description: The owner ID of the OAuth client (Port OS specific field)

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the OAuth client was created (Port OS specific field)

updatedAt.description: The timestamp when the OAuth client was last updated (Port OS specific field)
